stories.headline: Ranking the Premier League's best long-distance goals after Diego Gómez strike
stories.summary: Diego Gómez's long-range goal for Brighton vs. Palace was impressive, but which Premier League efforts are the best from history?
stories.body:
Diego Gómez added his name to an exclusive list of Premier League players who have scored goals from near the halfway line on Sunday afternoon, after walloping one in from long range in Brighton & Hove Albion's 5-0 demolition of Crystal Palace.

After receiving the ball in the center circle, the Paraguay international midfielder turned, spotted Palace keeper Walter Benítez off his line and proceeded to unleash a monstrous shot that sailed in from 55.7 yards.

That is the furthest out a goal has been scored in the Premier League since Wayne Rooney's similarly outrageous effort (63.4 yards) for Everton against West Ham United almost nine years ago.

Alongside Rooney, Gómez now joins some big names in the rundown of Premier League long-rangers. But how does his extraordinary strike against Palace stack up against the other raft of goals that have been scored around the halfway line?

14. Tim Howard (Everton) vs. Bolton Wanderers, 2012

The first of three goal-scoring keepers on the list, Howard successfully harnessed the power of the wind to score from inside his own area for Everton. While the distance was impressive, the goal loses several aesthetic points for being a freak, weather-assisted goal that bounced several times before hitting the back of the net.

13. Paul Robinson (Tottenham Hotspur) vs. Watford, 2007

Demonstrating his renowned set-piece mastery, Robinson scored for Spurs with a direct free kick from around 95 yards out when his aimless punt up field bounced high over the head of England rival Ben Foster and into the Watford goal.

12. Asmir Begović (Stoke City) vs. Southampton, 2013

The longest-distance goal in Premier League history (101 yards) was scored by Begović from inside his own penalty area with just 13 seconds of the game elapsed. The feat is certainly noteworthy, but the Bosnian was hugely assisted by a strong prevailing wind, a fortunate bounce, and the fact that his Saints counterpart, Artur Boruc, appeared to be playing in roller skates.

11. Xabi Alonso (Liverpool) vs. Newcastle United, 2006

After managing to evade an interfering referee, Alonso slung a speculative shot toward the Newcastle goal from the center circle that only really ended up in the back of the net thanks to the fact that goalkeeper Steve Harper's legs turned to jelly while trying to recover his position. Ingenious, but fairly low on style.

10. Stiliyan Petrov (Aston Villa) vs. Derby County, 2008

Villa thrashed Derby County 6-0 in what would prove to the latter club's Premier League annus horribilis, during which the Rams accrued a record low total of just 11 points. Petrov capped off the rout with a marvellously struck long-distance goal from the edge of the center circle.

9. Jonjo Shelvey (Swansea City) vs. Aston Villa, 2014

After bringing down an undercooked defensive clearance, Shelvey quickly assessed his options and chose to simply send the ball back from whence it came with an excellent long-range effort from the middle of the pitch.

8. Luis Suárez (Liverpool) vs. Norwich City, 2012

Suárez made a habit of terrorizing Norwich during his Liverpool days, but his longest-range goal against the Canaries came in 2012 when the Uruguay striker completed his hat trick from roughly 45 yards out.

7. Charlie Adam (Stoke City) vs. Chelsea, 2015

After the Stoke defense had quickly wrestled possession back from Chelsea, Adam was able to look up and launch a shot from midway inside his own half. Goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was able to get a flailing hand to the Scotland midfielder's effort, but couldn't prevent it from crossing the line.

6. Moisés Caicedo (Chelsea) vs Bournemouth, 2024

Scored on the final day of the 2023-24 season, Caicedo left it late to file his own entry for the Premier League goal of the season award with a 50-yard piledriver scored from the center spot. Unfortunately for the Chelsea midfielder, the actual award ended up going to Alejandro Garnacho for his overhead kick against Everton.

5. Wayne Rooney (Manchester United) vs West Ham United, 2014

Unusual in that it came from a bouncing ball, Rooney first demonstrated his ultra long-range prowess in 2014 when he dropped a spontaneous arching shot over bamboozled Hammers keeper Adrian from 45-plus yards out.

4. Maynor Figueroa (Wigan athletic) vs Stoke City, 2009

Reacting quickly to a free kick being given in his own half, Wigan full back Figueroa pounced on the opportunity to crack a 65-yard set piece soaring over the head of Stoke goalkeeper Thomas Sørensen in one fluid motion.

3. Wayne Rooney (Everton) vs West Ham United, 2017

A formidable and deceptively difficult first-time strike from Rooney that saw the ball sail with a perfect, flat trajectory over the head of stranded Hammers keeper Joe Hart, who had scurried out of his area to clear a loose ball.

2. Diego Gómez (Brighton & Hove Albion) vs Crystal Palace, 2026

It might not be the longest Premier League goal on record, but Gómez's ludicrous effort against Palace certainly ranks up there among the most technically adept. A beautifully flat, purposeful trajectory that rustled the net without bouncing. Bueno.

1. David Beckham (Manchester United) vs Wimbledon, 1996

The long-range Premier League strike by which all others are measured (literally, in some cases), Beckham's classic looping effort from the halfway line was famously achieved despite wearing someone else's boots on the very first day of the 1996-97 season and has since become the archetype of the genre.

stories.headline: Is Commanders coach Dan Quinn's job in jeopardy after tie with Giants?
stories.summary: Questions swirl Washington following last Sunday's embarrassing tie with the Giants. Where will they go from here?
stories.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn sat at a table deep inside Northwest Stadium, trying to make sense of a moment that made none. A coach known for wearing his hat backward instead wore a look of disbelief.

For the next 10 minutes, he tried to get comfortable. He folded his arms, then put them at his side, then put them back on the table. There was no comfort, not with what he had to address.

He took a quick deep breath after the first two questions, then readied for more. And more would come. There was no getting around what happened: a botched final sequence in his team's Week 5 matchup with the New York Giants prevented a game-winning field goal attempt on the final play, resulting in a 27-27 tie.

"Feels like a loss," Quinn said.

Inside the hushed locker room afterward, receiver Terry McLaurin stood against a burgundy cement wall. He looked upset; he looked drained; he looked bewildered. McLaurin, in his eighth season with the franchise, thought he'd seen it all in Washington -- but last Sunday brought something new.

"Unacceptable," McLaurin said.

With 50 seconds remaining in overtime, the Commanders had the ball at the Giants' 24-yard line with no timeouts. Then, all hell broke loose. They didn't snap the ball until there were 12 seconds to play. On the play, quarterback Jayden Daniels dropped back to pass and then quickly looked to scramble. He started upfield, then was tackled with nine seconds left. He did not get off the ground for another four seconds and there was little urgency by his teammates.

Once the final seconds had ticked away, Quinn slammed his headset to the ground, then stood at the 25-yard line, staring straight ahead as players headed to the locker room. Guard Sam Cosmi threw his helmet and kicked a pylon on his way inside.

The failed end-of-game operation led to a week of debate and questions: Did the players know they were out of timeouts? Who called the play? Why did it take so long? Why not spike the ball? It also led to an internal self-examination about what transpired. It also led to outside noise as analysts, fans and media discussed the play and assessed blame and a locker room that tried to shield itself from it all. It led to questions about Daniels and first-year offensive coordinator David Blough and, of course, Quinn's job status.

It also led to a reminder heard often for the team, now 1-3-1, during the week: There were still 12 games left, beginning with Monday night's matchup with the San Francisco 49ers (8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC).

"It's easy to come in and mope around," said running back Austin Ekeler, "but we can't do that because we still have a goal in front of us."

By Thursday, when they resumed practice, they had moved forward. But one former Commanders player said last week he would know from an outside perspective if the team had remained united by the message being delivered.

"If everyone says the same thing, you know they're in a good space," the player said. "If everyone says something different, then you might have an issue."

The message was the same throughout the week: They addressed the issue, said they were united and that they were moving on. But how quickly they can actually escape what happened remains to be seen.

As the former player said, "Winning cures all."

With 1:02 remaining, Commanders receiver Treylon Burks caught a pass, broke three tackles, turned upfield and ran out of bounds with 55 seconds left. The next play was a run that took five seconds. Then, 38 seconds elapsed before the next, and final, play was run.

The players on the field reacted to Daniels being tackles as if they had more than enough time remaining. Two players ran downfield routes. Their urgency in returning to the line of scrimmage, along with others on the field, was low. One of them, Burks, engaged verbally with the player covering him rather than sprint back.

The sequence left at least one player to wonder if some on the field had forgotten about the run play and thought the clock had been stopped. Multiple former play callers who did not want to be identified told ESPN they believed Washington -- Blough and the offensive players in particular -- didn't realize how much time had elapsed.

"It took so long in the huddle and they used motion," one former play-caller said. "I think they lost track of time."

One team source said the play call took too long to be relayed. After it was relayed, multiple team sources said it was surprising to see players being subbed in: They replaced two receivers with two tight ends. Then tight end Ben Sinnott went in motion from left to right and then back again, using more time.

Potentially compounding the issue, after the snap left guard Chris Paul stepped on Daniels' foot as he backed away from center. One player wondered if that messed up the timing for Daniels, increasing his urgency to run. An offensive coach from another team wondered the same, saying it then altered his drop and impacted the angle of the throw, causing Daniels to go into "panic mode."

Multiple players said they knew they were out of timeouts, which is why no one signaled for one after the sack.

Headset communication from the coaching staff to the quarterback cuts off with 15 seconds left on the play clock, and the lone voice talking to Daniels during this time is Blough, though Quinn is able to interject with his OC.

"If I'm the OC I'm asking the head coach, 'what do you want me to do?'" said one former defensive play-caller. "I'd tell them 'let's kill as much clock as we can or throw it out of bounds.' But whatever we do, we can't be tackled in-bounds with the ball."

"We learn," Blough said. "For me in particular, it's how do you handle that situation better the next time you're in it? It's a scar that we will all wear, but we go forward, man, and that's all you can do."

Up until the final play, Daniels was having a terrific game, posting 199 yards passing, 103 yards rushing and two touchdowns. That performance -- his first game playing with a brace on his left elbow that he dislocated in Week 2 -- provides hope, the last play notwithstanding.

As one player said, "If he plays like that, we have a chance."

Multiple players told ESPN that the team has not lost confidence in any of the parties involved -- Quinn, Blough, and Daniels especially.

Daniels briefly addressed the offensive players in a meeting last Monday, and one player said some clapped for him. Other teammates seated in the front row -- where Daniels always sits -- dapped him up after he spoke. The player said it was reminiscent of how they responded to him two weeks prior, when he told them that he'd return from a dislocated left elbow suffered in Week 2. Then, they clapped and cheered loudly. Some even stood, according to multiple people who were in the room.

Ultimately, Quinn, Blough and Daniels all accepted responsibility for the play -- both to the team and when addressing the media during their respective press conferences this week.

"It has been dissected, discussed and corrected internally. And that's where we'll stay," Quinn said.

During a panel on team ownership at The Economic Club in Washington, D.C. Thursday night, Harris referenced the "emotional rollercoaster" of being an owner. Sunday provided another reminder of an extreme low.

"I want to apologize to my wife for this last week," Harris told the crowd when discussing how it becomes an all-consuming familial pursuit. "I'm really sorry. It was a bad week, a bad Sunday. Look, that stuff stays with you."

Although the past seven days have been difficult for the organization, a source familiar with internal leadership conversations told ESPN that Quinn's job is not in immediate jeopardy and, the source said, that isn't likely to change during the season.

Ownership is aware of the support Quinn has in the locker room, the leadership source said, echoing what others said last season as well as this summer. They also know the team has been hit hard by injuries over the past two seasons and that with multiple players returning, or close to it -- and with a division that is seemingly up for grabs -- they want to see how this group responds.

It has been made clear multiple times since Josh Harris bought the team in 2023 that he does not like to change coaches during the season. He has fired two coaches with the NBA's Philadelphia 76ers -- Brett Brown and Doc Rivers, both after the season. Another coach, Doug Collins, resigned.

However, as owner of the NHL's New Jersey Devils, he has fired three coaches midseason. However, none had the first year Quinn had with Washington, taking the team to the NFC Championship Game in his first season. And, in each firing, they had been in charge for more than three seasons -- and other factors, such as whether or not they lost the locker room, were considered.

Ownership and other high-ranking members of the organization have long pointed to Quinn's leadership and team building as to why they remain behind him. They also felt Quinn did not lose the locker room last season, despite going 2-10 after a 3-2 start. They also did not discuss Quinn's job status with him before the season -- giving him no mandate as to what it would take to continue.

One player on the roster last season said the team also had "enough veteran presence that had been through stuff that they could say, 'Believe what this guy is saying.' And everybody believed. It was a close group. It allowed us to stay together. That doesn't mean it wasn't hard."

But, he said, knowing how players handled it in 2025 is why he doesn't think this gaffe "will break their confidence. I don't think inside is the issue; it will be outside."

Quinn has told people this week he still strongly believes in both first-year coordinators, Blough and Daronte Jones.

That doesn't mean Quinn and his staff receive a free pass. As one team source said, the losing would wear out anyone, including Harris. People who have worked for Harris say he separates emotion from his decision-making, but he's also not immune to feeling a certain way.

An ugly loss in San Francisco likely wouldn't change anything about Quinn's status, the source said.

Still, the Commanders are 6-15-1 since the start of last season and 3-13-1 in their last 17 games.

But, for now, they're not looking at the past.

"The sky is not falling right now," Cosmi said. "We've got 70 percent of our games to go. Put your head down, keep working, learn from your mistakes and push forward. All the opportunity is there to win the division."

stories.headline: Barcelona's Eric García, Jules Koundé ruled out of PSG clash with injury
stories.summary: Eric García and Jules Koundé have both been ruled out of Barcelona's Champions League game against Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday.
stories.body:
Eric García and Jules Koundé have both been ruled out of Barcelona's Champions League game against Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday.

García will also miss Sunday's Clásico against Real Madrid after being ruled out for up to four weeks with a thigh injury picked up in Saturday's win at Real Betis.

Koundé will be assessed ahead of Madrid's visit to Spotify Camp Nou in LaLiga this weekend after spraining his ankle in the same game.

The loss of García and Koundé leaves Barça coach Hansi Flick without either of the players he has used at right-back this season.

However, João Cancelo and Xavi Espart, both used as left-backs this year, can play there, as could Alejandro Balde.

García's injury also leaves Barça short at centre-back, with Andreas Christensen currently out with a thigh issue, too.

That leaves Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín as the only available central defenders in the squad ahead of Tuesday's showdown with the European champions.

Midfielders Rodri and Frenkie de Jong have also played there in the past, with Flick confirming the Dutchman could be an option at the back after he returned to training last week.

- 'Best in the world' Yamal propels Barcelona to record-equaling LaLiga start

- Manuel Pellegrini bemoans 'inexplicable decisions' as Real Betis lose to Barcelona

- Yamal vs. Mbappé: Which Clásico star has stronger claim to win the Ballon d'Or?

Elsewhere, following De Jong's return to the matchday squad at the weekend, Barça are in good shape ahead of the biggest week of their season so far.

Captain Raphinha returned off the bench against Betis and will be available for Tuesday's game in Paris and Madrid's visit on Sunday.

Barça are seeking to maintain their perfect start to the season in France after winning all 11 of their matches in all competitions to date.

stories.headline: How Kimi Antonelli can win F1 title at United States GP -- with or without Qatar, Abu Dhabi races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli, it's too late

- Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant Singapore drive

- Hamilton calls Singapore strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: Game 5 win has Rays on World Series cusp after wild weekend
stories.summary: The Rays beat the Guardians 3-1 on Sunday night to take a 3-2 lead in the ALCS.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- Bryan Baker, a quintessential Tampa Bay Ray, was about an hour removed from securing the most important out of his career to seal a quintessential 3-1 Rays victory in Game 5 of the American League Championship Series on Sunday when he found the words to describe the previous 72 hours for his ballclub.

"It was a wild few days, for sure," Baker said. "I think we handled it really well, though. We have all year."

Tampa Bay could not have handled it better. After losing Game 3, which was moved up five hours Thursday to avoid forecast inclement weather, to the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field to fall behind 2-1 in the series, the Rays waited out a postponement Friday to take Game 4 on a frigid Saturday night and Game 5 on Sunday, all in front of hostile sellout crowds.

The Rays did it Sunday by showcasing their brand of baseball. They pitched well behind a dominant start from ace Drew Rasmussen. They applied pressure offensively with their elite contact ability, speed and willingness to bunt -- and chased All-Star rookie starter Parker Messick out of the game after two innings. They played clean -- and at points outstanding -- defense. And now, with a 3-2 series lead, they'll have two cracks at advancing to the World Series for the third time in franchise history, starting with Monday's Game 6 back home at Tropicana Field.

"We have a great opportunity," Rays first baseman Yandy Diaz said in Spanish. "The guys are enthusiastic. And I think this ends tomorrow."

The Guardians, meanwhile, will face elimination again after overcoming a 2-0 deficit against the Chicago White Sox in the AL Division Series as they seek to win the franchise's first World Series title since 1948.

"In a way, it might be a blessing," Guardians catcher Austin Hedges said. "We play really good when it's like, 'OK, don't lose anymore.' It started last year. Then we did it again this year. For whatever reason, we love making things interesting. We might be up eight runs, but we'll find a way to make sure [closer] Cade Smith pitches.

"We keep it interesting for the fans. Now, we have to win. We're going to go play our best baseball now. I don't know why, but that's what we do. So in a way, I think the best is yet to come from us."

Friday's rainout erased Sunday's travel day and created the possibility of the series ending with games over four straight days. That prospect accentuated the importance of starting pitchers going deep into games to avoid overworking -- and overexposing -- their respective bullpens. So far, advantage Rays.

After using seven pitchers in a scheduled bullpen game Saturday, the Guardians needed six pitchers to get through the nine innings Sunday. Messick allowed two runs on five hits and threw 57 pitches in his two innings.

Diaz began the game with a leadoff double. Ryan Vilade later worked a walk before Chandler Simpson, one of the fastest players in the majors, beat out a ground ball to shortstop Brayan Rocchio with two outs to load the bases and keep the inning alive. Jonny DeLuca followed with a walk to score the game's first run before the Rays left the bases loaded.

The Rays manufactured their second run with singles from Liam Hicks, Diaz and Jonathan Aranda in the second inning. Messick was able to limit the damage to one run again, stranding two runners on base, but his night ended there.

"We didn't anticipate going into the bullpen in the third," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. "But with Parker at 60 pitches through two, it didn't feel right to put him back out there."

Like in the first inning, Simpson's speed produced a run for Tampa Bay in the third when he lined a double to right field against left-hander Tim Herrin before stealing third base and scoring on Hicks' bloop single to center field.

"It's just trying to create runs any way possible," said Rays shortstop Taylor Walls, who bunted for a hit to lead off the fourth inning before stealing second base and getting thrown out at home trying to score from second. "Some nights, it's going to be laying down bunts, getting guys over. Some nights, it's going to be a lot of contact. Some nights, it's going to be slugging and maybe hitting homers. But I think that we have the ability to create runs in multiple ways. We just don't know how it's going to happen that night."

Rasmussen and the bullpen ensured the squandered opportunities to blow the game open early was not a problem. The All-Star right-hander held Cleveland to one run on four hits over seven innings to add to his outstanding postseason. He struck out six, walked one and threw 95 pitches. In three playoff starts, including two in this ALCS, he has surrendered three runs across the 21 innings, good for a 1.29 ERA.

"Today, the way he limited anything was really, really impressive," Rays manager Kevin Cash said of Rasmussen.

Working with a better feel for his changeup than in Game 1, Rasmussen held the Guardians to one hit and a walk through five innings before finally encountering turbulence in the sixth. Steven Kwan and Jose Ramirez delivered back-to-back one-out singles before Chase DeLauter drove in Kwan with a groundout. Rasmussen then got Jo Adell to pop out to escape the jam.

"I feel like I say it every time that he pitches, but I mean, he's a dog," Simpson said of Rasmussen. "And every time he's out there, we know we got the best chance to win."

Cam Booser began the eighth inning and Tyler Wells ended it by striking out Ramirez with a runner at first base. Then Baker took over.

A year ago, the right-hander was a 30-year-old midseason acquisition with a 4.06 ERA. This year, behind a lethal fastball-changeup combination, he became one of the best relievers in the majors, posting a 1.44 ERA with 41 saves during the regular season. The All-Star is one of the Rays' many successful restoration projects over the years. And on Sunday, he finished off a classic Rays win and an unusual weekend to send them home with a chance to advance to the World Series.

"It's what we work for," Baker said. "It was a huge couple of games here to get us back in that spot. The first goal was just to get back to The Trop, and to be able to go back in this position is exactly what we wanted to do."

stories.headline: WNBA Finals 2026: Valkyries vs. Dream schedule, scores, more
stories.summary: A new champion is guaranteed to be crowned this season as Golden State and Atlanta meet in the WNBA Finals.
stories.body:
And then there were two. The No. 2 seed Golden State Valkyries and No. 4 Atlanta Dream will play in the WNBA Finals, a best-of-seven series that tipped off Saturday at Chase Center in San Francisco.

As the higher seed, Golden State will host Games 1, 2 and, if necessary, 5 and 7 in a 2-2-1-1-1 format.

The Dream announced Tuesday that they will host Games 3 and 4 at State Farm Arena, the home of the Atlanta Hawks. As part of the change, Game 3 also moved from Oct. 22 to Oct. 21.

The Dream's home arena, Gateway Center Arena, holds just 3,500 fans. Six of the Dream's regular-season games this season, and all three playoff games, have been played at State Farm, which seats more than 17,000 fans.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027? But hey, these were two sides I was down on this year and both ultimately outperformed expectations. Perhaps they do have it all figured out...

It's now or never

11. GOLD COAST

12. NORTH MELBOURNE

13. ST KILDA

If not now, then when? The Suns rocketed to co-flag favouritism this time last year after signing Christian Petracca and Jamarra Ugle-Hagan. They ultimately won just nine games and finished 13th on the ladder. Disastrous. Damien Hardwick is under serious pressure to get more out of this list. Meanwhile, the Kangaroos haven't played finals in a decade, but there's some newfound optimism after the senior coaching appointment of highly regarded Jaymie Graham and the signing of Nick Blakey, the biggest name the club has attracted in a decade. The Saints also need to show something early in 2027 or Ross Lyon could be on his way out ... again! But the real worry is not doing enough to ensure star midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera signs on.

It's going to be another long year

14. PORT ADELAIDE

15. GWS

16. WEST COAST

17. RICHMOND

18. ESSENDON

Perhaps I'm being a tad harsh on Port, who were pretty competitive this year. But at the end of the day we're taking Zak Butters out of a side that won just seven games. The Giants lost four of their best players in Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs, and will be relying heavily on their younger talent next year. And then there's the Eagles, Tigers, and Bombers -- three teams that combined for just nine wins this year. We all expect these sides to be somewhere around the bottom of the ladder.

stories.headline: Jasmine Jasudavicius outpoints Erin Blanchfield at UFC Fight Night
stories.summary: Jasmine Jasudavicius stated her case as a contender in the UFC women's featherweight division, dominating Erin Blanchfield on the canvas to win by unanimous decision.
stories.body:
Instability and opportunity permeate the UFC women's flyweight division, which crowned a new champion two weeks ago and has a former two-time champ lurking in the wings while healing from injury. Several other title hopefuls have been jostling to position themselves to go for the gold.

Jasmine Jasudavicius seized the opportunity to make her presence felt among the leading contenders Saturday, dominating Erin Blanchfield on the canvas in a clash of top-10 125-pounders to win by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night in Edmonton, Alberta.

The fight was the co-main event of a card headlined by Mike Malott's explosive knockout win over Joaquin Buckley. Malott, who like Jasudavicius is from Ontario and had the crowd firmly behind him, landed a knee to the chin that crumbled Buckley, who is No. 8 in the ESPN welterweight rankings and lost his third in a row.

"Hey, guys, I might be soft-spoken," Malott said afterward, "but I'm f---ing hard-hitting."

Malott's knockout came at 2 minutes, 32 seconds of the second round and put a ferocious cap on an event that tied a UFC record with 12 finishes (seven knockouts, five submissions). The other modern-era fight card with a dozen finishes was UFC Fight Night in Belgrade, Serbia, on Aug. 1.

Nevertheless, it was the night's lone bout to go the distance that had the highest stakes. Jasudavicius, No. 8 in the ESPN women's flyweight rankings, pulled off the upset against third-ranked Blanchfield, who came in situated behind only injured former champion Valentina Shevchenko and new titlist Natalia Silva. Blanchfield is also No. 9 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound top 10.

Jasudavicius (16-4) surely elevated her standing in the 125-pound hierarchy with a robust performance that produced her second straight victory.

Both women came in touted as elite grapplers, and Jasudavicius proved to be a step ahead by repeatedly taking the fight to the ground (five takedowns) and threatening submissions from dominant positions for long stretches of the first two rounds.

"I love grappling," she said. "I understand it. I'm pretty good at it. And I like to show what I've got."

Jasudavicius showed enough to impress the judges, getting the nod on all three scorecards (29-28, 29-28, 29-28). The announcement of the verdict drew a roar from the crowd, which was enthusiastically behind the 37-year-old competing in her home country.

"To be able to fight in Canada, you hear the crowd, man. We're about it," Jasudavicius said.

Jasudavicius and Malott were among a dozen Canadian fighters on the card who went a combined 5-7.

Jasudavicius' victory might not put her in position for an immediate title shot, but she has her sights on a future meeting with the new champion, who defeated her by decision in 2022 in her second UFC fight.

"I want to cross paths with Natalia Silva again," Jasudavicius said. "We had a little bit of history before, so it would be an epic story."

For Blanchfield (14-3), the defeat halted a two-fight winning streak. She outlanded Jasudavicius 62-43 in significant strikes, but the author of five UFC submissions never could get her ground game going. Jasudavicius put Blanchfield on the defensive the whole fight with nearly eight minutes of control time.

stories.headline: Lionel Messi scores twice, takes season tally to 25 in Miami win at Atlanta
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored two scintillating second-half solo goals to take his MLS-leading tally to 25 as Inter Miami brushed aside hosts Atlanta United 3-1 on Saturday.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi scored two trademark second-half solo goals to take his MLS-leading tally to 25 as Inter Miami brushed aside hosts Atlanta United 3-1 on Saturday.

After Mexico striker Germán Berterame put Miami ahead in the 45th minute, Messi took center stage after the restart with two goals in four minutes.

The first, in the 56th minute, came after Messi drove infield from the right wing and exchanged passes with Berterame on the edge off the penalty area before dancing past a desperate Atlanta defender and firing low into the net.

His second was more of the same. This time, Luis Suárez sent him free on a breakaway and the Argentine forward again bewitched a hapless defender before once more beating Atlanta goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos with his left foot.

Atlanta got a late consolation goal through a penalty from former Miami forward Fafà Picault.

"He never ceases to amaze the world," Miami coach Cristian "Kily" González said of Messi afterward. "I mean, I honestly can't believe that a guy like him, at 39 years old, is doing what he's doing. And what makes me happiest is seeing that he's truly happy. Because he's happy, he gives everything he has. He enjoys himself and feels right at home.

"As I always say, he pushes us to be better every single day. It's an immense joy to have him here. Everyone knows how special our relationship is. Every time I see him, he brings a smile to my face. I'm still constantly amazed by him."

At full time of Saturday's game, Messi had a six-goal lead in the race for MLS' Golden Boot and also had the joint-most assists (15), along with LAFC's Son Heung-Min, having been credited with a secondary assist on Berterame's opener.

Messi is the first player in MLS history to register 15 assists in three consecutive seasons. He now has a goal contribution in 13 straight matches, tying his second-longest streak with club and country in his career.

Saturday's brace also took Messi to 936 career goals, and his coach has no doubts that he can reach the 1,000 milestone.

"Yes, I believe he'll reach 1,000 goals," González said. "I have faith in that. I know he will, because he loves a challenge, he sets challenges for himself and since he's already achieved everything else, this will be no exception."

He added: "He dazzles me with every single action, every time I see him in training. I truly hope he continues to amaze us right up until the day he decides to retire, which, hopefully, won't be for a long time yet."

Messi's performance Saturday gave the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner another fond memory at Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The game marked Messi's first visit there since the 2026 World Cup semifinal in July, when he provided two late assists to propel Argentina to a dramatic win over England.

Messi has four goals in three games since he bid farewell to the Argentina national team in a friendly against Benin earlier this month.

Miami, which clinched a spot in the playoffs Wednesday, has won three straight games and is second in the Eastern Conference behind runaway leader Nashville.

Atlanta, under Gerardo "Tata" Martino, Messi's former coach with Miami and Argentina, is languishing in the 14th spot in the Eastern Conference and facing an uphill battle to make the postseason.

Miami will return to action with a visit to the New York Red Bulls next Saturday.

ESPN's Lizzy Becherano contributed to this report.

stories.headline: RLWC: What we learned from the opening round
stories.summary: Australia survived an opening-night scare, Tonga delivered a historic victory and Samoa wasted little time showcasing their attacking firepower. Isaac Issa takes a look atthe opening weekend of action.
stories.body:
Australia survived an opening-night scare, Tonga delivered a historic victory and Samoa wasted little time showcasing their attacking firepower.

The opening round of the 2026 Rugby League World Cup provided an early look at the contenders, while leaving England facing a difficult path to the knockout stages.

Here are the biggest takeaways from Week 1.

Australia win, but leave room for encouragement for their rivals

Australia banked the result they needed against New Zealand, but their 24-22 victory offered plenty for their rivals to work with.

The Kiwis gained close to 300 more running metres than the Kangaroos, exposing an area Australia will need to address as the tournament progresses. Winning a tight contest is valuable; consistently conceding that much ground is a difficult way to defend a World Cup.

Jack Bostock's debut hat trick proved decisive, while Reece Walsh's long-range try underlined Australia's ability to turn a game through individual brilliance. Those threats remain even when the Kangaroos are struggling to establish control.

For New Zealand, the frustration is that a strong performance went unrewarded. Kalyn Ponga's two tries demonstrated what he can add to their attack, although the arm injury that ended his night and left him needing surgery, raises concerns.

Australia emerged with the points. New Zealand showed enough to suggest another meeting would be far from straightforward.

Tonga's defence gives their title challenge substance

Tonga's attacking talent attracts attention, but their defensive resolve was the most significant feature of their 30-12 victory over England.

Repeatedly challenged in the opening half, Kristian Woolf's side held England scoreless and reached the break ahead 10-0. When AJ Brimson's try narrowed the gap, Tonga responded with consecutive tries to regain control.

Haumole Olakau'atu finished with a double as Tonga recorded their first victory over England.

The result strengthens their position in the race for a semifinal berth, but the manner of the performance should be just as encouraging.

Tonga demonstrated they could absorb pressure, withstand a shift in momentum and take their opportunities. Those qualities will become increasingly valuable when the tournament reaches its decisive matches.

Their ability with the ball was already apparent. Holding England out through that opening period provided a stronger indication of how difficult they could be to beat.

England already have little margin for error

One defeat has left England facing the prospect of an early exit, even if they win both remaining pool matches.

Only two teams from the combined Pool B and C standings advance to the semifinals. Tonga now hold the head-to-head advantage over England, while Samoa's 78-4 win over France has established a substantial points-difference buffer.

England still have France and Papua New Guinea to play. Winning those fixtures is the immediate requirement, but the size of those victories could also become crucial.

That creates a difficult balance: chasing points while correcting the errors that undermined their opener.

England generated opportunities against Tonga, yet too often failed to turn them into scoreboard pressure. Against opposition capable of punishing those missed chances, promising passages were insufficient.

Their next two performances must deliver considerably more. Even then, qualification could depend on results elsewhere.

Fa'alogo highlights Samoa's enviable attacking depth

Sua Fa'alogo began Samoa's World Cup opener on the bench. He finished it with four tries and 252 running metres.

Introduced after Deine Mariner suffered a hamstring injury, the Melbourne speedster immediately demonstrated the value of Samoa's attacking depth in their 78-4 win over France.

With Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow starting at fullback, Samoa could still call upon another explosive runner capable of transforming an opportunity into points. Fa'alogo's performance gives coach Ben Gardiner plenty to consider as the opposition becomes stronger.

There was encouragement beyond the established names, too. Test debutant Francis Manuleleua ran for 223 metres, including 89 after contact, while Jermaine McEwen topped Samoa's tackle count.

France offered limited resistance, so the result alone cannot establish where Samoa sit among the leading contenders.

It did, however, show how many attacking options they possess, and how difficult selection could become if their emerging players continue to contribute alongside their stars.

stories.headline: Noni Madueke on Arsenal's late win over stubborn Nottingham Forest: 'Champions' sprirt'
stories.summary: Arsenal forward Noni Madueke has said that the club showed the spirit of champions in their hard-fought Premier League win over Nottingham Forest on Sunday.
stories.body:
Arsenal forward Noni Madueke has said that the club showed the spirit of champions in their hard-fought Premier League win over Nottingham Forest on Sunday.

Forest had defended imperviously for most of the match and limited the Gunners to just one shot on target.

But Madueke broke the deadlock in the 80th minute, with his deflected strike earning Arsenal their 10th win in 11 games.

"This place is so hard to come to, everybody knows it," Madueke said after the match. "They make it so difficult for you. It was a really tough game.

"We showed grit, determination and I think we showed a champions' spirit here tonight."

Arsenal received some criticism for their blunt display against Forest, as they failed to create high-quality chances.

Head coach Mikel Arteta acknowledged that his side struggled to find the breakthrough and put it down to Forests' defensive shape, which he referred to as a "Christmas tree."

"We knew we wouldn't score in the first 20, 30 minutes. We weren't going to face a different Forest because they are extremely well coached. They put a Christmas tree there. There is no space to play. You have to be so neat and tidy.

- Mikel Arteta puts stale Arsenal display down to Nottingham Forest tactics: 'They put a Christmas tree there'

- Arsenal don't look ready to 'attack' the Premier League title like they want to -- yet

"You have to otherwise generate a lot of chaos in the box, whether it is in open play or with set-pieces.

"We did a couple of times and created two big chances. We didn't even hit the target, which is the difference.

"And the longer the game goes, we say, 'OK, now we have to play a different game because [at] the moment we start to ramp up our level of frustration.'

"But we got the goal."

Next up, Arsenal take on Bayern Munich in the Champions League at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Lisandro Martínez's Man United comments 'not that far off' but should not have been made - Peter Schmeichel
stories.summary: Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off."
stories.body:
Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off" but added he would not have liked hearing a teammate sound off in public.

Schmeichel was criticised for his handling of a post-match interview with Martínez in the aftermath of Tuesday night's 2-0 Champions League loss to Atlético Madrid, when the Argentina defender turned his fire on the club's hierarchy and named director of football Jason Wilcox as one of those from whom he "expects more."

Martínez spoke first to Amazon Prime's Gabriel Clarke before Schmeichel interviewed him for U.S. broadcaster CBS, with the defender repeating many of his criticisms while Schmeichel appeared to be trying to move Martínez on from the topic.

On Thursday Martínez issued a public apology for his comments and United said the matter was considered closed after the 28-year-old met with manager Michael Carrick, Wilcox and the club's hierarchy.

But inevitably the issue dominated Carrick's news conference on Friday with the substance of Martínez's comments still being debated.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Schmeichel said: "I would not like any teammate ever to go out and talk like that. Unless it was Bryan Robson... No, I wouldn't. I absolutely wouldn't like that.

"In the dressing rooms I was in, you were accountable. It just didn't happen very often that somebody stepped out of line, and of course we had a manager [Sir Alex Ferguson] who would not allow you to step out of line. He would react to that straight away...

"It's not that I completely disagree with what [Martínez] says. That's the other thing."

- Man United 'a circus' amid Lisandro Martínez rant - Roy Keane

Schmeichel then added: "Without going into too much detail about what Martínez said, some of the things he said are not far off.

"Look at the promising teams: Manchester City a long time ago, Arsenal for the past six years, Liverpool under Jürgen Klopp -- what did they do that suddenly changed the dynamics and changed their fortunes? They started at the back.

"They got in a goalkeeper, back four, a centre midfield player. They built that foundation, made it solid, and then they started to bring the creative players in. They've all done it... Built from the back. We've done the opposite, built from the front."

Formula 1 heads to Texas for the United States Grand Prix, with the championship battle set to heat up at the Circuit of the Americas.

Max Verstappen claimed his second victory this season after winning the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time.

Kimi Antonelli continued to extend his lead in the title championship to 102 points from Mercedes teammate George Russell, and there is a mathematical chance he will be able to clinch the title in Austin.

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

Circuit of the Americas

The Circuit of the Americas first hosted the United States Grand Prix in 2012, to mark the end of a five year wait since the race at Indianapolis.

Mario Andretti, who won the world championship in 1978, opened the track and it has become a popular race among drivers and fans alike with plenty of overtaking action and drama.

COTA is a varied circuit with straights, esses through to sector two, and a series of hair-pins in sector three. The high-speed corners takes some inspiration from Silverstone and Hockenheim.

It's a mix of fast corners, long straights and has one of the steepest elevation climbs to Turn 1.

The Red Bull driver dominated the race and posed as a serious threat to McLaren's Norris and Oscar Piastri in the drivers' championship.

Norris finished second and cut his lead to 14 points to Piastri in the standings, who finished fifth. Verstappen ended the weekend only 40 points behind Piastri with five races left of the season.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli will be as focused as ever to claim his ninth victory of the season with one hand already on the drivers' championship trophy.

However, Mercedes are still working on how to best optimise its current upgrade package. Last time out in Singapore, the team ran Russell on the older specification, while Antonelli had the upgraded package.

Red Bull were labelled by rivals as the "team to beat" for the remaining six races of the season. There seems to be no stopping Verstappen, who has won the U.S. Grand Prix four times.

Don't count out Hamilton who holds the record for six wins around COTA and will be looking to get his seventh podium for Ferrari this season.

stories.summary: With no travel day due to a Game 3 rainout, the weary Cleveland Guardians, who lost Game 5 of the ALCS Sunday at home to the Tampa Bay Rays, will face elimination Monday at Tropicana Field, but they have hope, given their 3-1 road record this postseason.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- Stephen Vogt and his Cleveland Guardians are used to this situation by now: needing two wins on the road to keep alive their season.

Cleveland faces a 3-2 deficit in the best-of-seven AL Championship Series and not a lot of time to rebound after Sunday's 3-1 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays. There is no travel day because of a rainout, and Game 6 is Monday night at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida.

"Let's go. We don't have another choice," Vogt said. "This is when this team thrives."

Cleveland rallied in September for the second straight season to win the AL Central. The Guardians were 60-65 and 5 1/2 games behind the Chicago White Sox in the AL Central on Aug. 17 before winning eight of nine and then going 16-9 in September to win the division by one game.

The Guardians dropped the first two AL Division Series games at home to the White Sox before winning the next two in Chicago and closing with a 2-0 win at Progressive Field in Game 5.

"I think it'll help a ton knowing that we're able to do it, facing elimination," said Steven Kwan, who had two of Cleveland's five hits and his first career postseason outfield assist. "I think we feel a little better on this one as opposed to the other ones since we've got some wins under our belt. Just have to trust our plans, turn the page and see what happens tomorrow."

Kwan, who has 51 career outfield assists in the regular season, threw out Taylor Walls trying to score from second base on Jonathan Aranda's fourth-inning single to left and made a leaping catch at the center-field wall on Victor Mesa Jr.'s eighth-inning drive, saving a run.

Teams trailing 3-2 after five games in the ALCS have come back to win only seven of 23 times. The last two teams in that position accomplished the feat, Texas in 2023 and Toronto last year.

Cleveland is 47-38 on the road in this year, including the postseason, and 43-44 at Progressive Field.

The biggest question is which pitcher will start Monday. Foster Griffin began Game 1 but was the bulk reliever for Game 4 on Saturday, working 3 2/3 innings and allowing one run and four hits.

Vogt ruled out right-hander Gavin Williams, who led the AL with 248 strikeouts in the regular season. Williams started Game 3 on Thursday and allowed two runs in five innings.

Cleveland's bullpen allowed only one run in seven innings after Parker Messick struggled. A candidate for AL Rookie of the Year, Messick had the shortest outing of his big league career and didn't make it past the third inning for the second time in four postseason starts.

The 25-year-old left-hander allowed two runs, five hits and three walks over two innings, throwing just 34 of 57 pitches for strikes.

Messick has pitched exactly 200 innings on the year, the first rookie to reach that mark in a season since Kansas City's Yordano Ventura at 208 1/3 innings in 2014. The prior Cleveland rookie to toss at least 200 innings was Charles Nagy with 211 1/3 innings in 1991.

"I feel great right now," Messick said. "Body feels good, arm feels good. I'm still throwing hard. I don't really have any body fatigue. It's just whether or not I'm executing the game plan."

stories.summary: Atlanta Dream (30-14, 15-5 Eastern Conference) at Golden State Valkyries (32-12, 15-8 Western Conference)
stories.body:
Atlanta Dream (30-14, 15-5 Eastern Conference) at Golden State Valkyries (32-12, 15-8 Western Conference)

San Francisco; Monday, 8 p.m. EDT

WNBA FINALS: Valkyries lead series 1-0

BOTTOM LINE: The Golden State Valkyries host the Atlanta Dream in the WNBA Finals with a 1-0 lead in the series. The Valkyries won the last matchup 68-64 on Oct. 17 led by 26 points from Gabby Williams, while Allisha Gray scored 19 points for the Dream.

The Valkyries have gone 17-5 in home games. Golden State is seventh in the Western Conference scoring 82.2 points while shooting 42.2% from the field.

The Dream have gone 15-7 away from home. Atlanta is the top team in the Eastern Conference with 43.7 points per game in the paint led by Angel Reese averaging 11.0.

Golden State averages 10.4 made 3-pointers per game, 2.3 more made shots than the 8.1 per game Atlanta gives up. Atlanta has shot at a 44.2% rate from the field this season, 2.8 percentage points greater than the 41.4% shooting opponents of Golden State have averaged.

TOP PERFORMERS: Veronica Burton is scoring 12.2 points per game with 3.6 rebounds and 5.7 assists for the Valkyries. Williams is averaging 19.3 points, 3.2 assists and 1.5 steals over the last 10 games.

Rhyne Howard is averaging 17.7 points, 3.7 assists and 2.3 steals for the Dream. Reese is averaging 18.1 points over the last 10 games.

LAST 10 GAMES: Valkyries: 8-2, averaging 81.8 points, 38.3 rebounds, 17.3 assists, 7.1 steals and 4.6 blocks per game while shooting 39.7% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 76.5 points per game.

Dream: 9-1, averaging 91.4 points, 33.9 rebounds, 21.5 assists, 9.8 steals and 3.6 blocks per game while shooting 43.5% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 77.2 points.

stories.headline: Griezmann has 2 goals, 1 assist for Orlando City in 4-1 win over DC United
stories.summary: Antoine Griezmann had two goals and an assist, Martín Ojeda added a goal and an assist, and Orlando City beat D.C. United 3-1 on Saturday night.
stories.body:
ORLANDO, Fla. -- - Antoine Griezmann had two goals and an assist, Martín Ojeda added a goal and an assist, and Orlando City beat D.C. United 3-1 on Saturday night.

Griezmann has 12 goals and seven assists in 14 MLS appearances and is the first player in league history with a goal contribution in 12 of his first 14 career games.

Marco Pasalić scored a stoppage-time goal for Orlando (12-13-5). Maxime Crépeau had three saves.

Tai Baribo converted from the penalty spot in first-half stoppage time for D.C. (7-10-12).

Ojeda, just inside the top of the 18-yard box, chipped a first-touch pass over four defenders to a charging Griezmann on the give-and-go for a first-touch finish from 7 yards out to make it 1-0 in the 15th minute.

Ojeda flicked a back-heel volley, off a feed from Griezmann, past goalkeeper Sean Johnson and inside the left post to give Orlando a two-goal lead in the 22nd.

Griezmann intercepted a misplayed pass by Kye Rowles in D.C.'s defensive third, took two dribbles and rolled a shot into the net to make it 3-1 in the 50th minute.

Johnson finished with three saves.

Up next D.C.: Plays Wednesday at Cincinnati.

Orlando: Hosts New York City next Saturday.
